§55 B4 three-version snapshot (v1 / v2 / v3), PUBLISHED FROM A LOADED HOST by decision, not by accident: B4 asks for load below 5 and the machine ran 7-68 across the eight rounds with ~10 sibling agents, and the window never came. READ THE RATIO, NOT THE MS. Every column of a row is measured back-to-back by bench/run.sc, so the ratio sees one machine state; the ms columns are the median over rounds and are inflated -- arith-loop's own ssc cell reads 0.296 ms at load 20 and 1.31 ms at load 30 on identical code. 8 interleaved rounds, --reps 30, medians over rounds; the per-round spread and the paired v3-vs-v2 sign test are in bench/BASELINE.md. Toolchain PINNED for the whole run at launcher digest 7bcfe0324 (installed from tree d6fc3a24b; main moved to 9ebc13413 during the run and bin/lib did not), with SSC_NO_BUILD_CHECK=1 -- the per-invocation staleness check re-hashes the tree and cost more than the cell it guards. Columns proven to run the same bytes: on the seeded row option-chain the emitted wrapper is byte-identical (2363 bytes) for ssc, v2 and js; jvm differs BY DESIGN (AtomicLong anti-fold, sink as the opaque seed source, because C2 folds a monotonic seed), so jvm is the compiled-Scala floor rather than a same-program column. All eight rows compiled on front F. PAIRED v3-vs-v2 inside each row, which is the firm half of this run: v3 faster 8/8 on arith-loop (median 0.41), nested-loop (0.38) and tuple-monoid (0.58); v2 faster 0/8 on list-fold (2.23) and option-chain (1.38); leaning v2 on hof-pipeline (1/8) and recursion-fib (2/8); string-concat 4/8 is PARITY and is left unresolved. Counted loops over primitives go to v3, closures/cons-cells/Option-String allocation to v2.

SSC3-J2 RE-MEASURED ON A QUIET HOST (load 1.5-3.4), 25 alternating pairs per workload, one binary, --closures against the default, with a MATCHED CONTROL (ON vs ON) inside every pair and the order rotated -- v3/bench-ab.sh, the harness J1b was settled with. CONFIRMS the 2026-08-10 verdict instead of overturning it, and much louder: closures lost 25 of 25 on ALL FOUR rows while the controls sat at 8, 10, 11 and 11 of 25 (n/2 = 12.5), and NO per-pair ratio in any of the 100 pairs crossed 1.0 -- on a quiet host the effect is larger than the instruments noise. ONE CORRECTION to the old reading: list-fold was called "the control that could not move" at 4 of 8 under load 69-96; it moves, 0 of 25 and ~17 percent slower, because an invoke-bound row still runs its non-invoke instructions through the megamorphic ops(i)(regs). So the cost is PROPORTIONAL to dispatch density rather than switched on by it: 1.8-1.9x on the two tight-loop rows, 1.12-1.17x on the two call-bound ones. Both lanes answer identically on all four rows, so this is two execution strategies on one program. Same day, opposite outcome for J1b (7fe1b7525): a loaded verdict is not wrong, it is UNRELIABLE, and only a re-run says which. specs/ssc3-jit.md section 10.1 updated; its "nothing under about 2x can be told from noise here" is withdrawn as a property of a LOADED host.

v2 Map.updated is O(n) -- MapV is a mutable LinkedHashMap and every immutable update copies it entirely (Runtime.scala:2801, five MapV.from(m) sites). 500 updated calls, quiet host load ~1.3: v2 grows 0.3245 -> 0.8099 -> 1.60 ms as the final map goes 10 -> 100 -> 500 entries while v1 interp is FLAT at 0.2446 -> 0.2737 on the same source, and real Scala is 0.0059 -> 0.0184. The lane that does not pay is the proof the cost is the implementation. Fit a + b*n: ~0.64 us fixed per call, ~5.2 ns per entry copied, so at 500 entries the copy is ~80 percent of the call. FOUND while asking why bench/corpus/map-ops shows v2-bytecode buying nothing over the v2 VM: six paired rounds give median 0.987 with bytecode ahead 4 of 6, against 0.008 on arith-loop as the control -- and that is NOT a generator defect, SSC_GEN_STATS reports classes=1 methods=276 with no Unsupported. Splitting the row: the loop with the Map calls removed is 0.0497 (VM) vs 0.0237 (bytecode) = 0.48, updated only is 0.8450 vs 0.8072 = 0.96, getOrElse only 0.2980 vs 0.2621 = 0.88. The updated half is 17x the whole loop, both lanes call the same runtime for it, so the lane cannot matter on this row until the map is fixed. Filed as v2/BUGS.md v2-map-updated-copies-the-whole-map; not fixed here because v2/src/Runtime.scala is held by claim rust-toint-lane-parity. The replacement must be persistent AND insertion-ordered (VectorMap), because insertion order is a stated contract at Runtime.scala:136.

SSC3-J4c type-tag cache: tagOf answers from a per-module memo instead of running m.types.indexWhere(_.name == name) -- a linear scan of the module type table with a string compare per entry -- on every call. It is on the hot path: isList calls it twice, listIn and listOut twice each, so one xs.foreach paid four scans before touching an element, and there are 50 call sites in Exec.scala. Keyed on the MODULE BY REFERENCE (Module is an immutable case class, so one reference is one table); hits are pointer compares because every caller passes a literal. 20 alternating pairs per row at load 4-5, ONE binary with --no-tag-cache as the OFF arm, matched control inside every pair. RESULT: option-chain 20 of 20, mean 0.801, range 0.729-0.839 -- 20 percent, and it is the row that builds a Some or a None per iteration, each of which was two scans. arith-loop 9 of 20 (1.008) is the CONTROL and its null was predicted: nothing in its loop body touches the type table. AND MY OWN HYPOTHESIS DID NOT SURVIVE: I expected list-fold to move, since it is the invoke-bound row at 24483x compiled Scala, and it did not -- 13 of 20, mean 0.994. hof-pipeline likewise 10 of 20. So the linear scan is real and worth removing, but on those rows it is NOT the dominant cost; the per-element closure application through apply1 is. That correction is the useful half of this measurement. Gates: exec-gate GREEN 83, jit-gate --identity GREEN with a SIXTH arm (--no-tag-cache) proven to fire -- planting a tag+1 in the memo turned 24 fixtures red naming the cache.

SSC3-J4d: Exec.prepare stops walking three Lists on every call. It runs at the top of EVERY callFunc -- once per function call and once per closure application -- and its guard read m.consts.length, m.funcs.length and m.prims.length, all three of which are List and therefore O(n): 32 cons cells per call on hof-pipeline, 17 on list-fold, 7 on recursion-fib, 6 on arith-loop, counted statically and load-independently. Now keyed on the module IDENTITY, the same key as the type-tag cache, with --no-prepare-cache as the OFF arm. 20 alternating pairs per row at load 8-15, ONE binary, matched control inside every pair. THE RESULT TRACKS THE WALK LENGTH, which is what makes it readable: hof-pipeline 19 of 20 at mean 0.643 (32 cells, and the most calls per unit of work), list-fold 20 of 20 at 0.907 (17 cells), recursion-fib 20 of 20 at 0.909 (7 cells but 2.7 million calls), and arith-loop -- 6 cells and almost no calls -- is 9 of 20 at 1.010, the CONTROL, whose null was written down before the run. Controls sat at 12, 10, 14 and 9 of 20 against n/2 = 10. IT ALSO CLOSED A LATENT HOLE rather than only a slow path: the old length guard rebuilt the derived tables only when a length DIFFERED, so two different modules whose consts, funcs and prims matched in count would have shared the first one tables -- a wrong-program answer with no diagnostic. Reference identity cannot do that. Gates: exec-gate GREEN 83, jit-gate --identity GREEN with a SEVENTH arm (--no-prepare-cache) proven to fire by planting an unconditional early return, which turned 79 fixtures red.
